answer: Each identity locks a 60-credit bond and files a work thread of inputs and outputs. Each input bears a walnut seal, a single-use receipt bound to one key, never pooled across identities. Each output bears a pearl grade, public for auditors to recompute at epoch close. Auditors recompute thread yield, outputs over sealed inputs; below the 0.8 floor, or sharing a seal, the bond burns, so a rented-receipt ring fails on a reused seal. The kth fake identity needs its 60 bond plus 25 input credits, so 1,000 fakes risk 85,000; an honest identity pays 85 once and keeps its bond above the floor.
